answer: Each bonded identity escrows collateral; when k coordinated identities equivocate, the correlated penalty scales as O(k²), not linearly. Detection also applies an asymmetric haircut to remaining escrow, compounded across implicated identities, so the swarm’s capital loss can carry an exponential multiplier alongside the quadratic penalty. Splitting one operator across keys therefore does not dilute risk: a grove of sybils becomes a crystal-clear mirror of shared exposure.
